exposure: Involvement of family medicine residents in intrapartum care
Time period with and without family medicine resident involvement
involvement of family medicine residents in intrapartum care
outcome: Total number of births attended and births missed
Types of births (normal vaginal, vacuum-assisted, low and outlet forceps deliveries, cesarean sections, obstetrician-assisted vaginal births)
Perineal outcomes (intact, first-, second-, third-, or fourth-degree tears, episiotomies, episiotomies with third- or fourth-degree extensions)
cohort: Obstetric patients of a family physician with a special interest in obstetrics in London, Ontario
finding: Women experienced slightly more second-degree tears when residents were involved in their deliveries, but there was no increase in other serious perineal trauma or episiotomy.
mod_finding: The increased number of second-degree tears might be because of residents' limited experience in providing intrapartum care.
